title_as_printed: Experimental Heat Capacity of Aqueous MgSO4 at 20 bar Pressure
pressure_note: flow calorimeter; pump pressure kept above the water vapour pressure so there is no vapour phase; 'All of the present results are for 20 bar' (title and text)

value.what: apparent molar heat capacity of MgSO4 calculated by the authors from the measured specific heat capacity of the solution and that of pure water

value2.what: massic (specific) heat capacity of the solution at T and 20 bar, from the measured heater-power ratio Ps/Pw with heat-loss correction and the 298 K density ratio (eq 1)

value3.what: density ratio of solution to water at 298 K used in eq 1 (flow rates equal by volume at 298.15 K); source of the densities not stated in the table

skip_rows.reason: temperature label rows (also carried by group_rows)

notes: Block labels printed as 'T = 348.15 K (75.0 degC)'; the degree sign is written as 'C'. Replicate rows (same m, repeated runs) kept. Authors' uncertainty in phiCp from the heat-loss assumption: 0.5 J/(K mol) at 2 mol/kg to 2.5 J/(K mol) below 0.5 mol/kg at 348 K, rising to 4 J/(K mol) at 423 K and 9 J/(K mol) at 473 K; total possible error up to double these values.
